diagrams.title: Medical Courier Launch Sequence
diagrams.subtitle: Contract first, vehicle second, reserves before direct invoicing

stages.label: Land the contract before the vehicle
stages.detail: No van or Sprinter purchase until a signed contract covers the payment; the car already owned is the launch vehicle (Medical Courier Connection).

stages.label: Carry HIPAA and bloodborne pathogen training
stages.detail: Practitioners treat HIPAA and bloodborne pathogen training as the baseline credential for any medical courier route.

stages.label: Bind commercial auto plus business liability
stages.detail: Diamond Hunter Enterprises: commercial auto insurance plus business liability insurance, even as a solo operator.

stages.label: Bank three months of operating expenses
stages.detail: Invoice-paid direct clients run 20-30 day billing cycles and first checks can take 90 days (Medical Courier Connection).

stages.label: Hire a driver only at a $300-$500 weekly spread
stages.detail: Hire only when $300-$500 a week remains after driver pay, and check the client contract for subcontractor and approval clauses first (Giganomic Era).

diagrams.caption: The launch order practitioners converge on: contract, credentials, insurance, cash reserves, then the first hire.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Sequence reflects the operator gates as stated; Sarah Davis notes that at levels one and two a name, SSN and 1099 status were enough to get hired before any LLC or EIN.
diagrams.note: Sources - Medical Courier Connection (o1VRiVMJTpY @ 00:24:07, 00:14:00); Diamond Hunter Enterprises (zQaL3OdQ2D8 @ 00:04:29); Giganomic Era (2w9s8G4Gx9Q @ 00:00:41).

diagrams.title: Dollar Stakes at Each NEMT Foundation Gate
diagrams.subtitle: From launch capital down to the portal fee, every gate carries a price

stages.label: Wheelchair-accessible van launch
stages.conversion: Launch capital sized before any enrollment filing
stages.detail: Geoff Cole's all-in figures; Medicaid enrollment then opens a 60 to 120 day dead zone with no billing.

stages.label: Missed state transport registration
stages.conversion: Medicaid office and transport authority are separate doors
stages.detail: Nemiton: enrollment is three separate layers; in California layer three is CPUC registration.

stages.label: Unregistered operation fines
stages.conversion: Registration filed and active before the first trip
stages.detail: Nemiton: operating without CPUC registration earned a cease and desist after 3 months on the road.

stages.label: Commercial auto premium
stages.conversion: Bound before trips, defense kept outside the limits
stages.detail: Brian Jungeberg on Medical Courier Connection; errors and omissions, not cargo coverage, protects a ruined biopsy.

stages.label: NC Tracks portal fee
stages.conversion: Portal link plus NPI required by most NC brokers
stages.detail: Motivational Charles: most brokers contacted required NC Tracks linkage and an NPI before paying a provider.

diagrams.caption: The LLC, EIN, Type 2 NPI, Medicaid enrollment and broker credentialing sequence, ranked by the dollars at stake at each gate.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Stage values use the upper bound of each quoted range; the $45,000 figure is a single operator's reported loss, not an average.

diagrams.subtitle: Direct retainers and routes against the vehicle-class ladder
diagrams.caption: Direct contracts set the floor; vehicle capacity widens the ceiling of what can be bid.

diagrams.title: Route Profitability Gates
diagrams.subtitle: No rate gets judged without miles, hours and volume attached

nodes.question: Are miles, hours, stops and daily volume known?
nodes.fail_action: Do not judge the rate; a $350 route at 250 miles and 10-12 hours can lose to a $250 route at 80 miles and 4 hours.

nodes.question: Is pay still positive after carrier deductions and fuel?
nodes.fail_action: Reprice or pass; $40 an hour with $8 an hour of gas is really $32 an hour, and settlements carry roughly $50 a week in deductions.

nodes.question: Are exclusivity, uncapped specimen liability and no-notice termination struck?
nodes.fail_action: Negotiate for 30 days notice minimum before signing.

nodes.question: Does the carrier contract allow subcontractors?
nodes.pass_next: Accept and price as a $175 flat daily rate built from $40 an hour, 70 cents a mile and a 25% markup.
nodes.fail_action: Walk away if the plan is to hire drivers and expand.

diagrams.caption: Four checks separate a paying route from a $20 job that costs $20 to handle.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The $175 daily rate is Giganomic Era's build for a 2.5-hour, 45-mile morning lab route; other routes need their own build.
diagrams.note: Sources - Sarah Davis | The D&G Way (hxoZsGym9DU @ 00:08:18); Samuel B. (X99grw6uMuY @ 00:03:30); Dean Medical Courier Academy (q25UyvVRKew @ 00:03:50); Giganomic Era (EgbN0cCrzpk @ 00:01:40, 00:06:19); Dj Mo (twmmoYWAs5Y @ 00:08:07).

diagrams.title: Single-Van NEMT Unit Economics Architecture
diagrams.subtitle: Selectivity, paid deadhead and priced wait time carry the margin

center.headcount: One multi-load wheelchair van on one broker contract
center.focus: Refuse $35 filler trips; the van grossed $125,000 in 2024 (ThatNEMTGirl).

spokes.kpi: Trips an hour or more out run only when the broker pays dead miles.
Base or load fee plus $2-$5 per mile and $15-$30 per 30 minutes of wait.
$500 per vehicle per week floor; about 200 trips at a $50 average for $10,000 a month.
Monthly expenses divided by monthly miles; reprice when rates stop covering it.

diagrams.caption: One van becomes a business when every spoke is measured against the owner's trip selectivity.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The $125,000 result came from a one-year test inside a five-vehicle fleet; the $500 weekly floor is Shantasia_RN's stated minimum, not disclosed earnings.
diagrams.note: Sources - ThatNEMTGirl (govQRXzu6Rg @ 00:01:22, 00:04:44); Shantasia_RN (3tRytphhdUU @ 00:01:00; Dr_9wzpyoaE @ 00:00:15); Nemt University (DoH4BLPOrvI @ 00:05:12).

diagrams.subtitle: The biggest jump comes from cutting out the middleman

buckets.label: Pharmacy fleet hourly route
buckets.notes: Unposted stat orders paying $80-$100 each can stack on top (Boss up with Kae).

buckets.label: Employee medical courier listing
buckets.notes: Pass unless the company vehicle is needed to get started (Ello Hunny Bun).

buckets.label: Direct facility contract
buckets.notes: Hospital pays the courier directly; three or more contracts reach $5,000-$9,000 a month (MONEY CENTRAL).

diagrams.caption: Same cooler, same specimens; the payer relationship decides which lane the hour lands in.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Direct facility pay is quoted as $28 to $65 an hour or more; STAT stacks only pay when the detour stays short, since a $50 STAT is not necessarily a $50 opportunity.

diagrams.title: Dispatch and Trip Verification Roadmap
diagrams.subtitle: A trip that cannot be proven will not get paid

weeks.title: Select broker-integrated dispatch software
weeks.deliverable: Fee stack compared, Bambi flat per-car pricing against RouteGenie at $50 per vehicle per month plus $100 setup, 2.5 cents per text and 5 cents per call.

weeks.title: Configure multi-load and bulk auto-dispatch
weeks.deliverable: Multi-loading enabled payer by payer with pickup and drop-off order set explicitly.
weeks.gate: Bulk assignment benchmark in reach, such as Bambi solving 41 trips in about 10 seconds.

weeks.title: Enforce six-point trip verification
weeks.deliverable: Service, recipient, provider, date, location, and start and end time captured with signatures, timestamps and GPS breadcrumbs.
weeks.gate: Any trip missing a point is held; breadcrumb mileage must match invoiced mileage.

weeks.title: Prove audit readiness and cut denials
weeks.deliverable: Automated reminders live and claim scrubbing on, the setup SwiftAid credits with cutting denials from 23% to 6%.
weeks.gate: Full audit packet of signatures, timestamps, routes and photos pulled in about 10 minutes.

diagrams.caption: Software, multi-load, verification and audit packets in sequence, as enforcement tightens around GPS-spoofed rides.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week labels sequence the work and are not practitioner-quoted durations; the denial and dispatch benchmarks are vendor and operator reports.
diagrams.note: Sources - Bambi (CbCgWxHPCxU @ 00:09:38; dxaejS8Bpis @ 00:00:15); RouteGenie (_mEgB7bAsFE @ 00:01:00; 382JPpV04Tg @ 00:01:09); SwiftAid Transport (YGC_f04Hg3g @ 00:08:34, 00:37:06); ZeitRide NEMT Software (ajqkD-2jPd8 @ 00:22:43).
